instruments.title: Add BankV, the Swiss Banking Ordinance (Bankenverordnung)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Verordnung über die Banken und Sparkassen (Bankenverordnung, BankV), SR 952.02, ordinance of the Federal Council under the Bankengesetz (BankG, SR 952.0) as a whole; consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Januar 2025, in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 70 Abs. 1: "Diese Verordnung tritt am 1. Januar 2015 in Kraft."

titles.de: Verordnung über die Banken und Sparkassen (Bankenverordnung, BankV)
titles.en: Banking Ordinance (Ordinance on Banks and Savings Banks)

payload.officialRef: Verordnung vom 30. April 2014 über die Banken und Sparkassen (Bankenverordnung, BankV), SR 952.02

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report every change to the facts behind the licence and get approval before material ones
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankV (SR 952.02), Art. 8a, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Report every change to the facts behind the licence and get approval before material ones

summaries.en: A bank, and a person licensed under Article 1b of the Banking Act, must report to FINMA every change in the facts on which the licence rests. Where a change is of material importance, FINMA's approval must be obtained before the activity is continued.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Separate lending, trading, asset management and settlement, regulate risk management and appoint an independent internal audit
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankV (SR 952.02), Art. 12 Abs. 1 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Separate lending, trading, asset management and settlement, regulate risk management and appoint an independent internal audit

summaries.en: A bank must effectively separate lending, trading, asset management and settlement inside the firm, and must lay down in regulations or internal guidelines the outline of its risk management and who approves risk-bearing business by what procedure, so that market, credit, default, settlement, liquidity, reputational, operational and legal risks are recorded, limited and monitored. It must document decisions on and monitoring of risk-bearing business so that the audit firm can form a reliable view, and must run an effective internal control system with an internal audit that is independent of management. FINMA may allow exceptions in justified cases.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Agree contracts under foreign law only where the counterparty recognises a stay of termination
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankV (SR 952.02), Art. 12 Abs. 2bis, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Agree contracts under foreign law only where the counterparty recognises a stay of termination

summaries.en: A bank must make sure, at the level of the single institution and of the group, that new contracts or changes to existing contracts that are governed by foreign law or name a foreign court are agreed only if the counterparty recognises a postponement of the termination of contracts under Article 30a of the Banking Act. FINMA may determine which kinds of contract need this.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give FINMA a business plan and the listed details before starting business abroad, and report later changes
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankV (SR 952.02), Art. 20, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Give FINMA a business plan and the listed details before starting business abroad, and report later changes

summaries.en: The notice a bank or a person licensed under Article 1b of the Banking Act gives FINMA before it becomes active abroad must hold everything needed to assess the activity: a business plan with the planned business and the organisation, the address of the office abroad, the persons entrusted with administration and management, the audit firm and the host supervisor. Giving up or materially changing the business abroad, and a change of audit firm or supervisor, must be reported as well.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Publish the annual report within four months and the half-yearly interim accounts within two months, and file both with FINMA
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankV (SR 952.02), Art. 31 und Art. 32 Abs. 1, 2 und 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Publish the annual report within four months and the half-yearly interim accounts within two months, and file both with FINMA

summaries.en: A bank must draw up interim accounts every half year, made up of a balance sheet and an income statement on the same basis as the annual accounts; a bank with listed equity or debt securities adds a statement of changes in equity and condensed notes. The annual report must be made available to the public, also in print, within four months of the closing date and the interim accounts within two months, and both must be filed with FINMA. Private bankers whose advertising does not cover deposit-taking are exempt from publication.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the systems, processes, depositor list and summary of other privileged deposits ready for a deposit payout
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankV (SR 952.02), Art. 42g und 42i, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Keep the systems, processes, depositor list and summary of other privileged deposits ready for a deposit payout

summaries.en: In its ordinary business a bank must keep an IT system and staff fit for its number of depositors, and standard processes that allow depositors to be contacted and their payment instructions collected and processed within the statutory deadlines. It must keep a depositor list of all secured deposits at its Swiss offices, in the format the deposit insurance scheme prescribes, from which the secured deposits per depositor can be established within 72 hours of a protective measure or of bankruptcy. It must also keep a summary of the privileged deposits that are not secured, with deposits at foreign offices shown as a total per jurisdiction.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Call publicly on entitled persons to claim assets that have been dormant for 50 years
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankV (SR 952.02), Art. 49, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Call publicly on entitled persons to claim assets that have been dormant for 50 years

summaries.en: A bank or a person licensed under Article 1b of the Banking Act must call on the entitled persons in public to claim, within one year, assets that have been dormant for 50 years; no publication is needed for assets of 500 francs or less. Where the details exist and no evident interest of the entitled person stands against it, the publication gives the address for claims, the person's name, date of birth and nationality or company name and last known domicile, and the account number where needed. It must say expressly that the costs of examining a claim may be charged to the claimant and that claims lapse when the assets are liquidated.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Describe in an emergency plan how systemically important functions continue, and update and file it every year
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankV (SR 952.02), Art. 60 Abs. 1, 2 und 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Describe in an emergency plan how systemically important functions continue, and update and file it every year

summaries.en: A systemically important bank must make sure that its systemically important functions can continue without interruption, independently of the rest of the bank, if insolvency threatens, and must take the measures this needs. It describes those measures in an emergency plan in which it proves to FINMA that it can do so, updates the plan every year by the end of the second quarter and files it with FINMA, and files an update whenever changes make a revision necessary or FINMA asks.

instruments.title: Add ERV, the Swiss Capital Adequacy Ordinance (Eigenmittelverordnung)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, ERV, SR 952.03, ordinance of the Federal Council under Art. 3 Abs. 2 Bst. b, 3g, 4 Abs. 2 und 4, 10 Abs. 4 Bst. a und 56 BankG and Art. 46 Abs. 3 und 72 FINIG; consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 24. Januar 2025, in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 151 Abs. 1: "Diese Verordnung tritt unter Vorbehalt der Absätze 2 und 3 am 1. Januar 2013 in Kraft." (Abs. 2: Art. 43 on 1 January 2016)

titles.de: Verordnung über die Eigenmittel und Risikoverteilung der Banken und Wertpapierhäuser (Eigenmittelverordnung, ERV)
titles.en: Capital Adequacy Ordinance (Ordinance on the Own Funds and Risk Diversification of Banks and Securities Firms)

payload.officialRef: Verordnung vom 1. Juni 2012 über die Eigenmittel und Risikoverteilung der Banken und Wertpapierhäuser (Eigenmittelverordnung, ERV), SR 952.03

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold the minimum own funds and the capital buffer, and tell FINMA and the audit firm when the minimum is no longer met
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, ERV (SR 952.03), Art. 42 Abs. 1 und 2 und Art. 43 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 24. Januar 2025

titles.en: Hold the minimum own funds and the capital buffer, and tell FINMA and the audit firm when the minimum is no longer met

summaries.en: A bank or account-holding securities firm must hold, after the prescribed deductions, Tier 1 capital of 3 per cent of its total exposure and own funds of 8 per cent of its risk-weighted positions, and on top of that a permanent capital buffer as set in Annex 8 to the ordinance. It must inform FINMA and its audit firm as soon as it no longer has the minimum own funds.

payload.refLabel: Art. 42 Abs. 1 und 2 und Art. 43 Abs. 1

obligations.title: Add the duty: Prove adequate own funds to FINMA every quarter, and every half year on a consolidated basis
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, ERV (SR 952.03), Art. 14, consolidated German text, Stand am 24. Januar 2025

titles.en: Prove adequate own funds to FINMA every quarter, and every half year on a consolidated basis

summaries.en: A bank must show every quarter that it has adequate own funds, in the statement whose content FINMA defines, and every half year on a consolidated basis. The statements are filed with FINMA within six weeks of the end of the quarter or half year.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Inform the public about risks and own funds
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, ERV (SR 952.03), Art. 16 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 24. Januar 2025

titles.en: Inform the public about risks and own funds

summaries.en: A bank must inform the public in an appropriate way about its risks and its own funds, and the calculation of its eligible own funds must be traceable from its accounts. Private bankers who do not publicly solicit deposits are exempt; FINMA sets the technical detail.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Identify and monitor large exposures and keep each within 25 per cent of Tier 1 capital
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, ERV (SR 952.03), Art. 95 und Art. 97 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 24. Januar 2025

titles.en: Identify and monitor large exposures and keep each within 25 per cent of Tier 1 capital

summaries.en: A bank must identify and monitor large exposures, which arise when its total position towards one counterparty or a group of connected counterparties reaches 10 per cent of its adjusted eligible Tier 1 capital, and other large credit risks. A single large exposure may not exceed 25 per cent of that capital; the limit does not apply to positions towards central banks, central governments and supranational organisations, positions they expressly guarantee or secure with financial collateral, or clearing positions towards qualified central counterparties.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report large exposures to the board every quarter and send the report to the audit firm and FINMA within six weeks
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, ERV (SR 952.03), Art. 100 Abs. 1 bis 8, consolidated German text, Stand am 24. Januar 2025

titles.en: Report large exposures to the board every quarter and send the report to the audit firm and FINMA within six weeks

summaries.en: A bank must report all large exposures and other large credit risks to its body for direction, supervision and control every quarter on a single-entity basis and every half year on a consolidated basis, and send the report on FINMA's form to its audit firm and to FINMA within six weeks of the end of the period. The report covers every large exposure and every position of 10 per cent or more of eligible Tier 1 capital before risk mitigation or without a limit, once a year the twenty largest total positions, each before and after risk mitigation. Exposures to members of the bank's bodies, qualified shareholders and persons close to them, and to group companies, are marked as such.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report a large exposure above the limit at once and clear it within a short period FINMA approves
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, ERV (SR 952.03), Art. 101, consolidated German text, Stand am 24. Januar 2025

titles.en: Report a large exposure above the limit at once and clear it within a short period FINMA approves

summaries.en: A bank that finds a large exposure above the limit without an exception applying must report it without delay to its audit firm and to FINMA and bring it back within the limit in a short period, which FINMA must approve. Excesses that arise only from trade-date accounting and settle within the next two bank working days, or three because of foreign holidays, need not be reported at once.

instruments.title: Add LiqV, the Swiss Liquidity Ordinance (Liquiditätsverordnung)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, LiqV, SR 952.06, ordinance of the Federal Council under Art. 4 Abs. 2, 10 Abs. 4 Bst. a und 56 BankG and Art. 46 Abs. 3 und 72 FINIG; consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Januar 2025, in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 33 Abs. 1: "Diese Verordnung tritt unter Vorbehalt der Absätze 2 und 3 am 1. Januar 2013 in Kraft." (Abs. 2: Art. 5 to 10 for banks that are not systemically important on 1 January 2014)

titles.de: Verordnung über die Liquidität der Banken und Wertpapierhäuser (Liquiditätsverordnung, LiqV)
titles.en: Liquidity Ordinance (Ordinance on the Liquidity of Banks and Securities Firms)

payload.officialRef: Verordnung vom 30. November 2012 über die Liquidität der Banken und Wertpapierhäuser (Liquiditätsverordnung, LiqV), SR 952.06

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set a liquidity risk tolerance, run liquidity stress tests and keep a contingency plan for liquidity shortages
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, LiqV (SR 952.06), Art. 2, Art. 6, Art. 9 Abs. 1 und Art. 10, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Set a liquidity risk tolerance, run liquidity stress tests and keep a contingency plan for liquidity shortages

summaries.en: A bank or account-holding securities firm must at all times have enough liquidity to meet its payment obligations in stress as well, and hold a sufficient and lasting liquidity reserve. It defines how much liquidity risk it is willing to take, sets its strategies accordingly, takes liquidity costs and risks into account in pricing, new products and performance measurement, and runs stress tests on several scenarios; banks of categories 4 and 5 use only the scenario of the short-term ratio. It draws up a contingency plan with effective strategies for liquidity shortages and fixes responsibilities, communication channels and measures in internal guidelines.

payload.refLabel: Art. 2, Art. 6, Art. 9 Abs. 1 und Art. 10

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the liquidity coverage ratio at 1 or more, in all currencies and in Swiss francs
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, LiqV (SR 952.06), Art. 12 Abs. 1 und Art. 14 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Keep the liquidity coverage ratio at 1 or more, in all currencies and in Swiss francs

summaries.en: A bank must hold enough high-quality liquid assets to cover at any time the net cash outflow expected over 30 calendar days in the stress scenario the ordinance defines, so that the ratio of the two is at least 1. The ratio must be met separately at the level of the financial group and of the single institution, for all positions across all currencies converted into Swiss francs and for the positions in Swiss francs.

payload.refLabel: Art. 12 Abs. 1 und Art. 14 Abs. 1 und 2

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell FINMA at once when the liquidity coverage ratio is missed or about to be, and present a plan to restore it
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, LiqV (SR 952.06), Art. 17b Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Tell FINMA at once when the liquidity coverage ratio is missed or about to be, and present a plan to restore it

summaries.en: The required level of the liquidity coverage ratio may be undershot for a time when extraordinary circumstances cause a drastic shortage of liquidity. A bank must notify FINMA without delay when the required level is undershot or an undershoot is in sight, and promptly submit a plan that shows by which measures and by when the level will be reached again.

obligations.title: Add the duty: File the liquidity statement monthly and the funding statement quarterly with the Swiss National Bank
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, LiqV (SR 952.06), Art. 17c Abs. 2 bis 4 und Art. 17q Abs. 2 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: File the liquidity statement monthly and the funding statement quarterly with the Swiss National Bank

summaries.en: A bank that is not systemically important must file its liquidity statement with the Swiss National Bank every month within 20 calendar days of month end, and its funding statement every quarter within 60 calendar days of quarter end, or every half year if it is in category 4 or 5. A systemically important bank files the liquidity statement monthly within 15 calendar days and the funding statement monthly within 30 calendar days. The positions are valued on the accounts drawn up under the accounting rules, on the forms FINMA determines.

payload.refLabel: Art. 17c Abs. 2 bis 4 und Art. 17q Abs. 2 bis 4

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the net stable funding ratio at 1 or more
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, LiqV (SR 952.06), Art. 17f und Art. 17h Abs. 1, 2, 4 und 5, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Keep the net stable funding ratio at 1 or more

summaries.en: A bank must keep its funding stable over a one-year horizon, so that the net stable funding ratio is at least 1, at the level of the financial group and of the single institution for all positions across all currencies converted into Swiss francs. Where FINMA lets Swiss institutions of a group meet the ratio together, each must still show a ratio of at least 0.8 on its own, and an institution with material domestic systemically important functions must always meet the ratio on its own.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Publish the liquidity position and the liquidity coverage ratio regularly
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, LiqV (SR 952.06), Art. 17e Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Publish the liquidity position and the liquidity coverage ratio regularly

summaries.en: A bank must regularly inform the public in an appropriate way about its liquidity situation and its liquidity coverage ratio. A systemically important bank discloses the ratio as the daily average of the last 90 days, or of the last 180 days where it discloses only every half year.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report the totals of deposits, privileged deposits and secured deposits to FINMA each year
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, LiqV (SR 952.06), Art. 18 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Report the totals of deposits, privileged deposits and secured deposits to FINMA each year

summaries.en: As part of its general reporting a bank must report to FINMA the total of the deposits shown in its balance sheet at the close of the financial year, the part of them that is privileged under Article 37a of the Banking Act and the part of those that is secured under Article 37h. FINMA uses the secured amount to calculate each bank's contribution obligation to the deposit insurance scheme.

instruments.title: Add FINIV, the Swiss Financial Institutions Ordinance (Finanzinstitutsverordnung)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Verordnung über die Finanzinstitute (Finanzinstitutsverordnung, FINIV), SR 954.11, ordinance of the Federal Council under the Finanzinstitutsgesetz (FINIG, SR 954.1) as a whole; consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Januar 2025, in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 94: "Diese Verordnung tritt am 1. Januar 2020 in Kraft."

titles.de: Verordnung über die Finanzinstitute (Finanzinstitutsverordnung, FINIV)
titles.en: Financial Institutions Ordinance

payload.officialRef: Verordnung vom 6. November 2019 über die Finanzinstitute (Finanzinstitutsverordnung, FINIV), SR 954.11

obligations.title: Add the duty: Lay down the organisation and the exact scope of business, employ qualified staff and cover the whole business with risk management
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIV (SR 954.11), Art. 12, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Lay down the organisation and the exact scope of business, employ qualified staff and cover the whole business with risk management

summaries.en: A financial institution must lay down its organisation in its organisational documents and describe its field of business precisely, by subject and by geography, in line with its financial means and its operational organisation. It must have staff that is adequate for its business and qualified for it, and a risk management that covers the whole business so that all material risks can be identified, assessed, steered and monitored.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Put each delegation of tasks into a written agreement, record it in the organisational documents and keep it open to audit
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIV (SR 954.11), Art. 17, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Put each delegation of tasks into a written agreement, record it in the organisational documents and keep it open to audit

summaries.en: A financial institution stays responsible for meeting its supervisory duties when it delegates tasks and must protect its clients' interests. It agrees with the third party, in writing or another form that allows proof by text, which tasks are delegated, and settles the powers and responsibilities, any right to sub-delegate, the third party's duty to account and the institution's rights of control; it records the delegated tasks and any sub-delegation in its organisational documents. The delegation must be set up so that the institution, its internal audit, the audit firm, the supervisory organisation and FINMA can inspect and audit the delegated task.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give FINMA a business plan and the listed details before starting business abroad, and report later changes
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIV (SR 954.11), Art. 18, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Give FINMA a business plan and the listed details before starting business abroad, and report later changes

summaries.en: The notice a financial institution gives FINMA before it becomes active abroad must hold everything needed to assess the activity: a business plan with the planned business and the organisation, the name and address of the office abroad, the persons entrusted with administration and management, the audit firm and the foreign supervisor. It must also report to FINMA when it gives up or materially changes the business abroad and when the audit firm or the foreign supervisor changes.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Run a securities firm with at least two managers, risk management and compliance apart from trading, and an independent internal audit
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIV (SR 954.11), Art. 66 Abs. 1 bis 3 und Art. 68 Abs. 1 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Run a securities firm with at least two managers, risk management and compliance apart from trading, and an independent internal audit

summaries.en: A securities firm must be able to be represented by a member of its management or supervisory body who lives in Switzerland, and its management body must have at least two persons. It must have adequately resourced risk management and effective internal control that secure compliance in particular, set the outline of its risk management and its risk tolerance, and separate the risk management and compliance functions by function and hierarchy from the operating units, trading above all. Client dealers and market makers must also have a separate body for direction, supervision and control and an internal audit that is independent of management, with sufficient resources and unrestricted audit rights.

payload.refLabel: Art. 66 Abs. 1 bis 3 und Art. 68 Abs. 1 bis 4

obligations.title: Add the duty: Record orders and trades in securities and in derivatives on them, for own account and for clients alike
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIV (SR 954.11), Art. 74 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Record orders and trades in securities and in derivatives on them, for own account and for clients alike

summaries.en: A securities firm must record every order it receives and every transaction it carries out in securities. The duty also covers orders and transactions in derivatives whose underlying securities are admitted to trading on a trading venue or DLT trading facility, and it applies to business for the firm's own account and for clients' account alike.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report every trade in securities admitted to a trading venue, with the beneficial owner's identification
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIV (SR 954.11), Art. 75, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Report every trade in securities admitted to a trading venue, with the beneficial owner's identification

summaries.en: A securities firm must report every transaction it carries out in securities admitted to trading on a trading venue or DLT trading facility, and in derivatives on them, for its own account or for clients: the name and number of securities bought or sold, the volume, date and time, the price and the details that identify the beneficial owner. Certain trades carried out abroad need not be reported, namely those of a foreign branch or foreign participant that is authorised to trade and subject to reporting there where the Swiss venue is informed regularly, and trades in foreign securities on a recognised foreign venue. Third parties may be used to file the reports.

instruments.title: Add FIDLEV, the Swiss Financial Services Ordinance (Finanzdienstleistungsverordnung)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Verordnung über die Finanzdienstleistungen (Finanzdienstleistungsverordnung, FIDLEV), SR 950.11, ordinance of the Federal Council under the Finanzdienstleistungsgesetz (FIDLEG, SR 950.1) as a whole; consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Januar 2022, in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 112: "Diese Verordnung tritt am 1. Januar 2020 in Kraft."

titles.de: Verordnung über die Finanzdienstleistungen (Finanzdienstleistungsverordnung, FIDLEV)
titles.en: Financial Services Ordinance

payload.officialRef: Verordnung vom 6. November 2019 über die Finanzdienstleistungen (Finanzdienstleistungsverordnung, FIDLEV), SR 950.11

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell clients what the service and the instruments are, what risks they carry and what they cost
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEV (SR 950.11), Art. 7 und 8, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2022

titles.en: Tell clients what the service and the instruments are, what risks they carry and what they cost

summaries.en: A financial service provider's information must cover the nature of the service, how it works and the client's main rights and duties, the risks of the service (for transaction advice the instruments concerned, for asset management and portfolio advice the risks of the investment strategy) and the general risks of the financial instruments, with their features and possible losses and obligations. It must give the one-off and running costs of the service and the costs of buying or selling instruments; costs that cannot be fixed in advance are given approximately or as ranges, and if that is not possible either, this is disclosed with a warning of further fees, taxes or costs. Where the details are in the key information document or the prospectus, handing over or pointing to that document is enough.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the information in good time, and to retail clients on a durable medium or a website
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEV (SR 950.11), Art. 12 bis 14, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2022

titles.en: Give the information in good time, and to retail clients on a durable medium or a website

summaries.en: The information the ordinance requires must be made available to a retail client on a durable medium or on a website; on a website it must be retrievable, downloadable and storable at any time, and the client must be told the address and the place where it is found. Clients must be informed early enough to understand the information before the contract is concluded or the service provided. Information on risks and costs is given when the contract that opens the client relationship is concluded or before the service is first provided.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep records that allow an account to the client within ten working days, and render it on a durable medium
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEV (SR 950.11), Art. 18 und 19, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2022

titles.en: Keep records that allow an account to the client within ten working days, and render it on a durable medium

summaries.en: A financial service provider must organise its documentation so that it can as a rule account to a client for the services provided within ten working days. The account covers the orders received and executed, the composition, valuation and development of the portfolio in asset management, the development of the portfolio where a custody account is managed, and the costs it has to disclose. It is given on a durable medium at the intervals agreed with the client and on the client's request.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set criteria for choosing the execution venue, prove compliance on request and review the criteria every year
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEV (SR 950.11), Art. 21, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2022

titles.en: Set criteria for choosing the execution venue, prove compliance on request and review the criteria every year

summaries.en: To secure the best possible result for the client, a financial service provider must set the criteria for choosing the execution venue for client orders, in particular price, costs, speed and the likelihood of execution and settlement; an express instruction from the client is followed. On the client's request it shows that the client's orders were executed in line with the criteria, and it reviews the effectiveness of the criteria at least once a year.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set internal rules for the conduct duties, select staff carefully and train them, and monitor compliance
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEV (SR 950.11), Art. 23, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2022

titles.en: Set internal rules for the conduct duties, select staff carefully and train them, and monitor compliance

summaries.en: Unless special statutory rules apply to it, a financial service provider meets its duties under the Financial Services Act by defining internal rules that fit its size, complexity, legal form, services and risks, by selecting its staff carefully and by making sure they receive the training on the conduct rules and the specific expertise their tasks need. Where a business unit has several persons, it also ensures effective monitoring through adequate internal controls and defines binding work and business processes.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Take organisational measures against conflicts of interest and disclose the conflicts that cannot be avoided
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEV (SR 950.11), Art. 25 und 26, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2022

titles.en: Take organisational measures against conflicts of interest and disclose the conflicts that cannot be avoided

summaries.en: A financial service provider must take measures, proportionate to its risks, size and services, to detect conflicts of interest, to prevent or monitor exchanges of information that could run against clients' interests, to separate staff whose main tasks could conflict, to keep remuneration from creating incentives to disregard duties or harm clients, and must issue and regularly review internal directives, including rules on staff dealing for their own account. Where a disadvantage to clients cannot be prevented or only at disproportionate cost, it discloses this by describing in general but understandable terms the circumstances of the conflict, the risks for the client and the measures taken to reduce them. The disclosure may be standardised and electronic, and the client must be able to store it on a durable medium.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Never churn client portfolios, front-run client orders, manipulate issues or settle at a price other than the one achieved
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEV (SR 950.11), Art. 27, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2022

titles.en: Never churn client portfolios, front-run client orders, manipulate issues or settle at a price other than the one achieved

summaries.en: A financial service provider may in no case reshuffle clients' custody accounts without an economic reason in the client's interest, exploit information, in particular knowledge of client orders, for own-account dealing by staff or the firm before, alongside or after those orders, manipulate services in connection with issues or placements of financial instruments, or settle a client order at a price that differs from the price actually achieved.

instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Verordnung über die Finanzmarktinfrastrukturen und das Marktverhalten im Effekten- und Derivatehandel (Finanzmarktinfrastrukturverordnung, FinfraV), SR 958.11, ordinance of the Federal Council under the Finanzmarktinfrastrukturgesetz (FinfraG, SR 958.1) as a whole; consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Januar 2025, in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 135: "Diese Verordnung tritt am 1. Januar 2016 in Kraft."

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report every trade in securities admitted to a trading venue, with the beneficial owner's identification
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraV (SR 958.11), Art. 37, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Report every trade in securities admitted to a trading venue, with the beneficial owner's identification

summaries.en: A participant admitted to a trading venue must report every transaction it carries out in securities admitted to trading on a trading venue, and in derivatives on them, for its own account or for clients: the name and number of the securities, the volume, date and time, the price and the details that identify the beneficial owner. Certain trades carried out abroad need not be reported, namely those of a foreign branch or foreign participant that is authorised to trade and subject to reporting there where the Swiss venue is informed regularly, and trades in foreign securities on a recognised foreign venue. Third parties may be used to file the reports.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report a derivative yourself when the other party is exempt or when you stand nearer the central counterparty
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraV (SR 958.11), Art. 92 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Report a derivative yourself when the other party is exempt or when you stand nearer the central counterparty

summaries.en: A derivative transaction with a party that is exempt from the derivatives trading rules must be reported by the counterparty that is subject to the act. Centrally cleared transactions traded on a trading venue or organised trading facility are reported by the counterparty that stands nearer to the central counterparty in the chain, subject to the act's rule on foreign counterparties.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Confirm the terms of an OTC derivative by the second business day after the trade
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraV (SR 958.11), Art. 95, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Confirm the terms of an OTC derivative by the second business day after the trade

summaries.en: The counterparties must confirm the terms of an OTC derivative transaction to each other by the second business day after it was concluded, or by the third where it was concluded after 4 p.m.; for complex transactions and small counterparties the deadlines are one business day longer. They may agree that a transaction counts as confirmed when one of them does not object to the confirmation.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Agree portfolio reconciliation before trading OTC derivatives and reconcile daily, weekly or quarterly by number of trades
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraV (SR 958.11), Art. 96, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Agree portfolio reconciliation before trading OTC derivatives and reconcile daily, weekly or quarterly by number of trades

summaries.en: The arrangements for reconciling portfolios must be agreed before an OTC derivative transaction is concluded, and the reconciliation covers the material terms of the transactions and their valuation. It is carried out every business day where 500 or more OTC derivative transactions are outstanding between the counterparties, once a week where between 51 and 499 are outstanding at any time in the week, and once a quarter where 50 or fewer are outstanding at any time in the quarter. A third party may carry it out.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Agree jurisdiction, governing law and dispute procedures at the latest when an OTC derivative is concluded
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraV (SR 958.11), Art. 97, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Agree jurisdiction, governing law and dispute procedures at the latest when an OTC derivative is concluded

summaries.en: The counterparties must agree the place of jurisdiction and the governing law for disputes at the latest when an OTC derivative transaction is concluded. The agreement sets procedures to identify, record and monitor disputes over the recognition or valuation of the transaction and the exchange of collateral, recording at least how long the dispute lasts, the counterparty and the amount in dispute, and procedures to settle disputes swiftly, with a special process for those not settled within five business days.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Exchange variation margin, and initial margin once the group's uncleared OTC derivatives exceed 8 billion francs
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraV (SR 958.11), Art. 100, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Exchange variation margin, and initial margin once the group's uncleared OTC derivatives exceed 8 billion francs

summaries.en: Where counterparties have to exchange collateral, they do so as an initial margin against price moves while a position is closed out and replaced after a default, and as a variation margin against current price moves after the trade. Only counterparties whose aggregated month-end average gross position in OTC derivatives not cleared through a central counterparty, at the level of the financial or insurance group or the group of companies, exceeds 8 billion francs for March, April and May of a year must post initial margin, and then for the whole of the following calendar year.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Write down the procedures that secure the derivatives duties
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraV (SR 958.11), Art. 113, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Write down the procedures that secure the derivatives duties

summaries.en: Financial and non-financial counterparties must set out, in writing or another form that allows proof by text, the procedures by which they secure their duties on central clearing, on determining the thresholds, on reporting to a trade repository, on risk mitigation and on trading on trading venues and organised trading facilities. A non-financial counterparty that does not want to trade derivatives may record that decision in the same form and is then exempt; a financial counterparty that carries out these duties for others sets out the procedures accordingly.

instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Verordnung über die kollektiven Kapitalanlagen (Kollektivanlagenverordnung, KKV), SR 951.311, ordinance of the Federal Council under the Kollektivanlagengesetz (KAG, SR 951.31) as a whole; consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 25. November 2025, in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 145: "Diese Verordnung tritt am 1. Januar 2007 in Kraft."

titles.en: Collective Investment Schemes Ordinance

obligations.title: Add the duty: Deal with a fund only at market price and do not charge twice for delegated services or related target funds
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKV (SR 951.311), Art. 31 Abs. 1 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 25. November 2025

titles.en: Deal with a fund only at market price and do not charge twice for delegated services or related target funds

summaries.en: Persons who manage or keep Swiss collective investment schemes or manage or represent foreign ones, and their agents, may buy investments from a scheme for their own account, or sell it investments from their own holdings, only at the market price. They must waive the remuneration due to them for services they delegated to third parties unless it is used to pay the third party, may charge no costs when investments are transferred between schemes of the same or a related licence holder, and may charge no issue or redemption commission when they acquire target funds that they manage themselves or that a company connected to them manages.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Separate asset management decisions, trading and settlement, and administration
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKV (SR 951.311), Art. 33 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 25. November 2025

titles.en: Separate asset management decisions, trading and settlement, and administration

summaries.en: Persons who manage or keep Swiss collective investment schemes or manage or represent foreign ones, and their agents, must effectively separate the activities of deciding (asset management), carrying out (trading and settlement) and administration. FINMA may allow exceptions in justified cases or order further functions to be separated.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Point investors to the risks and disclose every cost, the use of the management fee and distribution compensation
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKV (SR 951.311), Art. 34, consolidated German text, Stand am 25. November 2025

titles.en: Point investors to the risks and disclose every cost, the use of the management fee and distribution compensation

summaries.en: Persons who manage or keep Swiss collective investment schemes or manage or represent foreign ones, and their agents, must point investors in particular to the risks of a given type of investment and disclose all costs of issuing and redeeming units and of managing the scheme, the use of the management commission and any performance fee. The information on compensation for distribution covers the kind and amount of all commissions and other monetary benefits. When they exercise membership and creditor rights they must be transparent enough for investors to follow how the rights were exercised.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Staff the custodian bank function with at least three full-time signatories and keep each fund's assets and records apart
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKV (SR 951.311), Art. 102a und Art. 104 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 25. November 2025

titles.en: Staff the custodian bank function with at least three full-time signatories and keep each fund's assets and records apart

summaries.en: A custodian bank must have an organisation fit for its tasks, with adequately qualified staff and at least three full-time positions with signing authority for the custodian activity. It is responsible for the fund's accounts and custody accounts but may not dispose of the assets on its own, ensures that the countervalue of transactions is transferred within the usual time and otherwise notifies the fund management and claims replacement from the counterparty, and keeps records and accounts that at all times distinguish the assets held for each scheme. For assets that cannot be taken into custody it verifies the ownership of the fund management company or the scheme and keeps records of it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Check and monitor every third-party or central custodian the fund's assets are passed to
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKV (SR 951.311), Art. 105a, consolidated German text, Stand am 25. November 2025

titles.en: Check and monitor every third-party or central custodian the fund's assets are passed to

summaries.en: Where a custodian bank passes the safekeeping of fund assets to a third-party or central securities depository in Switzerland or abroad, it must check and monitor that the custodian has the operational organisation, financial guarantees and professional qualifications the assets require and is subject to regular external audit that confirms the financial instruments are in its possession. It must also check that the custodian keeps the assets so that regular reconciliations identify them at all times as belonging to the fund, and that it observes the rules that bind the custodian bank on delegated tasks and on avoiding conflicts of interest.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Run a liquidity management process for every fund, with regular stress tests and a crisis plan
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKV (SR 951.311), Art. 108a Abs. 1 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 25. November 2025

titles.en: Run a liquidity management process for every fund, with regular stress tests and a crisis plan

summaries.en: A fund management company or SICAV must secure, through a process, the appropriate management of liquidity for every scheme it manages: the liquidity profile of the investments fits the investment policy, the redemption terms and the liabilities, liquidity is monitored continuously and considered in investment decisions, suitable liquidity management tools are provided for, and the information needed to judge liquidity is at hand. It must run appropriate stress tests at regular intervals on normal and exceptional market conditions, which may be omitted where the scheme's net assets are 25 million francs or less. It must draw up a crisis plan with the measures, procedures and internal responsibilities for using the tools, and review the plan regularly.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Do not end a business relationship of your own accord once a suspicion must be or is being reported
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV (SR 955.01), Art. 12a, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Do not end a business relationship of your own accord once a suspicion must be or is being reported

summaries.en: A financial intermediary may not end a business relationship on its own initiative when the conditions for a report under Article 9 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act are met or when it uses the right to report under Article 305ter(2) of the Criminal Code. Where there are concrete signs that the authorities are about to secure assets, it may neither end a relationship for which it decides not to use the right to report although the conditions are met, nor allow significant assets to be withdrawn.

obligations.title: Add the duty: End a reported business relationship only in the listed cases and let significant assets leave only with a paper trail
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV (SR 955.01), Art. 12b Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: End a reported business relationship only in the listed cases and let significant assets leave only with a paper trail

summaries.en: Apart from the case the act itself provides for, a financial intermediary may end a reported business relationship where the reporting office tells it within 40 working days that the information goes to a prosecution authority and no order from that authority arrives within five working days, where no such order arrives within five working days of a report under Article 9(1)(c) of the act, or where it is told that a freeze ordered by a prosecution authority has been lifted. If it ends a relationship for which it decided not to use the right to report although the conditions were met, it may allow significant assets to be withdrawn only in a form that lets the prosecution authorities follow their trail.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep a record when another financial intermediary is told that a suspicion was reported
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV (SR 955.01), Art. 12c, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Keep a record when another financial intermediary is told that a suspicion was reported

summaries.en: A financial intermediary that informs another financial intermediary that it has filed a report under Article 9 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act or Article 305ter(2) of the Criminal Code must record that fact in a suitable form.

obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, MGwV (SR 955.23), Art. 3 Abs. 1 und 1bis, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Give every suspicious activity report the content the ordinance lists

summaries.en: A financial intermediary's report to the Money Laundering Reporting Office must name the intermediary with a direct telephone number of the person in charge and its supervisory body, and give the identification details of the contracting party and of the beneficial owner, other persons authorised to sign or represent, the assets involved with the current balance, as exact a description as possible of the business relationship with its number and opening date, and the documented grounds for suspicion with account statements, supporting documents, links to other relationships and the result of the clarifications made. A report that a reported relationship was ended carries the same details apart from the supervisor and the grounds, and in addition the office's reference number of the original report, proof of the termination and its date, and the paper trail of significant assets withdrawn.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Exchange information with the reporting office through its information system, after registering in it
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, MGwV (SR 955.23), Art. 3a, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Exchange information with the reporting office through its information system, after registering in it

summaries.en: Information is exchanged with the Money Laundering Reporting Office through the information system the office provides. Every user of the system must register in it beforehand.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Provide the key information document of a qualified life insurance in good time on a durable medium or a website
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AVO (SR 961.011), Art. 129d, consolidated German text, Stand am 26. Februar 2026

titles.en: Provide the key information document of a qualified life insurance in good time on a durable medium or a website

summaries.en: An insurer must make the key information document of a qualified life insurance available to policyholders on a durable medium or on a website, early enough for them to understand it before the contract is concluded or the service provided. On a website the document must be retrievable, downloadable and storable at any time, and the policyholder must be told the address and the place where it is found.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Check that a qualified life insurance is affordable, fits the client's risk capacity and suits the term the client needs
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AVO (SR 961.011), Art. 129m, consolidated German text, Stand am 26. Februar 2026

titles.en: Check that a qualified life insurance is affordable, fits the client's risk capacity and suits the term the client needs

summaries.en: When checking whether a qualified life insurance is appropriate for the policyholder, the insurer or the insurance intermediary must check in particular whether the client can afford it financially, whether its risk profile matches the client's capacity to bear risk and whether its term fits the client's life situation and investment objectives. Where the policyholder acts through an authorised representative, the representative's knowledge and experience are taken into account.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep records of qualified life insurance business that allow an account within ten working days
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AVO (SR 961.011), Art. 129n und 129o, consolidated German text, Stand am 26. Februar 2026

titles.en: Keep records of qualified life insurance business that allow an account within ten working days

summaries.en: Insurers and insurance intermediaries must organise their documentation of qualified life insurance business so that they can account to policyholders within ten working days. The account is given on a durable medium at the intervals agreed with the policyholder or on request.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Meet the untied intermediary rules when appearing untied, keep free of insurer ties and report changes in the registered facts
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AVO (SR 961.011), Art. 182b, Art. 182c Abs. 1 und Art. 185 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 26. Februar 2026

titles.en: Meet the untied intermediary rules when appearing untied, keep free of insurer ties and report changes in the registered facts

summaries.en: Anyone who gives policyholders the impression of acting as an untied insurance intermediary must meet the requirements for untied intermediaries. An untied intermediary may not be bound by agreements that limit its freedom to work for other insurers, hold more than 10 per cent of an insurer's capital or, through its managers or holders of more than 10 per cent, hold a leading function in or otherwise influence an insurer, and no insurer may hold more than 10 per cent of it or influence it in those ways. A registered intermediary must report to FINMA every change in the facts behind its registration and obtain FINMA's approval before continuing where the change is material.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep consumer credit interest at or below the three-month compounded SARON plus 10 percentage points
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VKKG (SR 221.214.11), Art. 1 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Juli 2021

titles.en: Keep consumer credit interest at or below the three-month compounded SARON plus 10 percentage points

summaries.en: The maximum interest rate for consumer credit is the three-month compounded SARON plus 10 percentage points, rounded to the nearest whole number and never less than 10 per cent. For overdrafts on a current account and for credit and customer cards with a credit option the surcharge is 12 percentage points, and the maximum never less than 12 per cent.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Use the consumer credit information system's data only for the creditworthiness check
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VKKG (SR 221.214.11), Art. 3 Abs. 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Juli 2021

titles.en: Use the consumer credit information system's data only for the creditworthiness check

summaries.en: The information system of the information office for consumer credit makes available only the personal data that commercial lenders and crowdlending brokers need for the creditworthiness checks under Articles 28 to 30 of the Consumer Credit Act. Those data may be processed only for that purpose.

instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Verordnung über den Datenschutz (Datenschutzverordnung, DSV), SR 235.11, ordinance of the Federal Council under Art. 8 Abs. 3, 10 Abs. 4, 12 Abs. 5, 16 Abs. 3, 25 Abs. 6, 28 Abs. 3, 33, 59 Abs. 2 und 3 DSG; consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. titles.en: Data Protection Ordinance

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set risk-based technical and organisational measures for the confidentiality, availability, integrity and traceability of personal data
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSV (SR 235.11), Art. 1 und Art. 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Dezember 2025

titles.en: Set risk-based technical and organisational measures for the confidentiality, availability, integrity and traceability of personal data

summaries.en: A controller and a processor must determine how much protection the personal data need, assess the risk to the persons concerned and set appropriate technical and organisational measures, taking account of the state of the art and the cost, and review all three over the whole processing period. The measures must ensure access, entry and user control, control of data carriers, storage and transport, quick restoration after an incident, availability, reliability and integrity of the systems, up-to-date operating systems and software with known critical gaps closed, and controls that show who entered, changed or disclosed which data and when. Breaches of data security must be detected quickly and their effects reduced or removed.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Log storage, change, disclosure, deletion of and access to sensitive data processed on a large scale, and keep the logs for a year
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSV (SR 235.11), Art. 4 Abs. 1, 3, 4 und 5, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Dezember 2025

titles.en: Log storage, change, disclosure, deletion of and access to sensitive data processed on a large scale, and keep the logs for a year

summaries.en: Where a private controller or its processor processes sensitive personal data on a large scale by automated means or carries out high-risk profiling, and preventive measures cannot ensure data protection, it must at least log the storing, changing, disclosing, deleting and destroying of the data and access to them. The logs show who processed the data, what was done, the date and time and any recipient. They are kept for at least one year separately from the system that processes the data, and only those who check data protection or data security may see them and only for that purpose.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep an up-to-date regulation for automated processing of sensitive data on a large scale or high-risk profiling
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSV (SR 235.11), Art. 5, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Dezember 2025

titles.en: Keep an up-to-date regulation for automated processing of sensitive data on a large scale or high-risk profiling

summaries.en: A private controller and its processor must draw up a regulation for automated processing where they process sensitive personal data on a large scale or carry out high-risk profiling. The regulation describes in particular the internal organisation, the processing and control procedures and the data security measures; it must be updated regularly and given to the data protection adviser where one is appointed.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Put the required points into data protection clauses and specific guarantees for transfers abroad and make sure recipients keep them
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSV (SR 235.11), Art. 9 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Dezember 2025

titles.en: Put the required points into data protection clauses and specific guarantees for transfers abroad and make sure recipients keep them

summaries.en: Data protection clauses in a contract and specific guarantees used for disclosing personal data to a country without adequate protection must at least cover the processing principles, the categories of data and persons, the kind and purpose of the disclosure, the countries concerned, retention and deletion, the recipients, data security, the duty to report breaches, the duty of recipient controllers to inform the persons concerned, and the rights of those persons. The controller, and the processor where the clauses are in its contract, must take appropriate measures to make sure the recipient observes them.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Notify a data security breach with the listed details, inform the persons concerned plainly and document every breach for two years
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSV (SR 235.11), Art. 15, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Dezember 2025

titles.en: Notify a data security breach with the listed details, inform the persons concerned plainly and document every breach for two years

summaries.en: A notification of a data security breach to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner must state the kind of breach, as far as possible its time and duration and the categories and approximate number of data and persons affected, the consequences and risks for the persons concerned, the measures taken or planned and a contact person; missing details follow as soon as possible. Where the persons concerned must be informed, the controller tells them in simple language at least the kind of breach, its consequences, the measures and the contact. The controller must document every breach with the facts, effects and measures and keep the documentation for at least two years from the notification.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Answer access requests in an understandable form within 30 days after identifying the requester
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSV (SR 235.11), Art. 16 Abs. 2 bis 5 und Art. 18, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Dezember 2025

titles.en: Answer access requests in an understandable form within 30 days after identifying the requester

summaries.en: A controller gives access in writing or in the form in which the data exist, electronically if wished, and always in an understandable form, after taking appropriate measures to identify the person asking. Access must be given within 30 days of receiving the request; if that is not possible, the controller tells the person by when it will follow, and a refusal, restriction or postponement must be communicated within the same period.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Register with the Federal Tax Administration by the end of the year in which reporting starts, and deregister by the end of the year it ends
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AIAV (SR 653.11), Art. 31 Abs. 1, 2 und 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2026

titles.en: Register with the Federal Tax Administration by the end of the year in which reporting starts, and deregister by the end of the year it ends

summaries.en: A Swiss financial institution or relevant reporting crypto-asset service provider must register with the Federal Tax Administration at the latest by the end of the calendar year in which it becomes a reporting Swiss financial institution or relevant reporting provider. It must deregister by the end of the calendar year in which that status ends or the business is given up; telling the administration that it holds no reportable accounts or has no reportable users is not a deregistration. A trustee registering a trust adds "TDT=" before the trust's name.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Name the currency of every amount in the account reports
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AIAV (SR 653.11), Art. 26, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2026

titles.en: Name the currency of every amount in the account reports

summaries.en: A reporting Swiss financial institution must state in its reports the currency in which the amounts are given. It may give them in the currency of the financial account, in the reference currency the account holder chose, in Swiss francs or in US dollars.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep a cover register with an inventory of every cover item and a journal of every change
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, PfV (SR 211.423.41), Art. 11 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Keep a cover register with an inventory of every cover item and a journal of every change

summaries.en: A member bank of a Pfandbrief central institution must keep its cover register as an inventory that lists for each cover item at least the register and business number, the nominal amount, date and reference of the mortgage title, the debtor, the amount of the pledged claim, prior ranking, the cover value, location and kind of the pledge, the land area, the estimated value, the lending limit and remarks on changes, and as a journal of every entry and every increase or decrease of pledged claims and cover with the totals. Supplementary cover is kept in a separate inventory with its kind, nominal value, market price and cover value, and the bank must make sure the cover is assured at all times even if items leave unexpectedly. A bank that stores the amounts electronically and can retrieve them at any time may do without the journal.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the cover of Pfandbriefe and loans apart from other assets, marked and held safely in Switzerland
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, PfV (SR 211.423.41), Art. 14, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Keep the cover of Pfandbriefe and loans apart from other assets, marked and held safely in Switzerland

summaries.en: The cover of Pfandbriefe and of the central institutions' loans must be separated from all other assets, marked as cover, split into ordinary and supplementary cover and kept in a safe place in Switzerland. Physical cover may be kept together with other assets only where it can be separated and blocked at once on the order of the central institution, the audit firm or the supervisor. Third-party custody or fiduciary administration is allowed only where the custodian or fiduciary waives every security and retention right over the cover, which must be proved to the central institution on request.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep loan cover of at least 110 per cent of nominal value and 108 per cent after lending limits at all times
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, PfV (SR 211.423.41), Art. 14b, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Keep loan cover of at least 110 per cent of nominal value and 108 per cent after lending limits at all times

summaries.en: The nominal value of a member's loan cover must at all times be at least 110 per cent of the nominal value of the loans from the Pfandbrief central institutions, or 115 per cent where the pool holds mortgage claims granted outside the member's internal affordability rules. The value of the cover counted within the lending limits must at all times be at least 108 per cent of the loans' nominal value; FINMA may set a higher level.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Publish cover pool data every half year within two months of the interim closing date
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, PfV (SR 211.423.41), Art. 21a, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Publish cover pool data every half year within two months of the interim closing date

summaries.en: A Pfandbrief central institution must publish at least every half year, within two months of the interim closing date, the value of the Pfandbriefe and of the cover, the breakdown of the cover pool by location and kind of property and by size of claim, the interest income of Pfandbriefe and cover, the currency risk, the maturity structure of Pfandbriefe and cover, and the share of cover claims more than 90 days overdue.

instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Verordnung zum Bundesgesetz über die Schweizerische Nationalbank (Nationalbankverordnung, NBV), SR 951.131, ordinance of the Swiss National Bank under Art. 15 Abs. 3, 17 Abs. 2, 18 Abs. 5, 20 Abs. 3 und 23 Abs. 1 NBG; consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. obligations.title: Add the duty: Answer the National Bank's statistical surveys truthfully, on time, free of charge and in the prescribed form
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, NBV (SR 951.131), Art. 5 Abs. 1 und Art. 8 Abs. 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. November 2026

titles.en: Answer the National Bank's statistical surveys truthfully, on time, free of charge and in the prescribed form

summaries.en: The annex to the ordinance sets for each statistical survey its subject, who must report, the reporting unit, the frequency and the deadline. A person obliged to report must give the information truthfully, within the deadline, free of charge and in the prescribed form.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold Swiss franc coins, notes and sight deposits at the National Bank of 4 per cent of the relevant liabilities on average
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, NBV (SR 951.131), Art. 12, 13 und 15, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. November 2026

titles.en: Hold Swiss franc coins, notes and sight deposits at the National Bank of 4 per cent of the relevant liabilities on average

summaries.en: Only banks must hold a minimum reserve; banking groups that hold liquidity collectively meet it at group level. The reserve is 4 per cent of the average of the three month-end values of the relevant liabilities before the period, and must be met on average over each period from the 20th of a month to the 19th of the next with circulating Swiss coins, banknotes and sight deposits at the National Bank, counted daily at close of business.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report minimum reserve compliance to the National Bank by month end and pay interest on any shortfall
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, NBV (SR 951.131), Art. 16 und 17 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. November 2026

titles.en: Report minimum reserve compliance to the National Bank by month end and pay interest on any shortfall

summaries.en: A bank must report to the National Bank by the end of the month in which a period closed that it met the minimum reserve requirement, in the form the National Bank sets. A bank that falls short pays interest on the shortfall for the days of the period at 4 percentage points above the average overnight Swiss franc rate based on SARON, and at least 500 francs.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Capture, limit and monitor money laundering risks across foreign branches and group companies
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV-FINMA (SR 955.033.0), Art. 6 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Capture, limit and monitor money laundering risks across foreign branches and group companies

summaries.en: A financial intermediary with branches abroad or at the head of a financial group with foreign companies must record, limit and monitor its money laundering and terrorist financing risks globally: an independent unit periodically prepares a consolidated risk analysis, branches and group companies report in a standardised way at least once a year and inform it of their most significant relationships, transactions and changes in risk, and the group compliance function runs risk-based checks on site. It must make sure that its internal control bodies and the group audit firm can obtain information on single relationships in all branches and group companies when needed, and it informs FINMA without delay where access to information on clients or beneficial owners in a country is excluded or seriously hindered.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Refuse assets from crime and relationships with terrorist financiers, criminal organisations and shell banks
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV-FINMA (SR 955.033.0), Art. 7 Abs. 1 und Art. 8, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Refuse assets from crime and relationships with terrorist financiers, criminal organisations and shell banks

summaries.en: A financial intermediary may not accept assets that it knows or must assume come from a felony or a qualified tax offence, even one committed abroad. It may not maintain business relationships with companies or persons it knows or must assume finance terrorism or form, belong to or support a criminal organisation, or with banks that have no physical presence where they are incorporated, unless they belong to a financial group under appropriate consolidated supervision.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Put the originator's and beneficiary's details into every payment order and handle incomplete orders on a risk basis
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV-FINMA (SR 955.033.0), Art. 10 Abs. 1, 2, 4 und 5, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Put the originator's and beneficiary's details into every payment order and handle incomplete orders on a risk basis

summaries.en: The originator's financial intermediary must give in a payment order the originator's name, account number and address and the beneficiary's name and account number, or a transaction reference where there is no account; the address may be replaced by date and place of birth, client number or national identity number. The originator details must be accurate and complete and the beneficiary details complete; within Switzerland the account number or reference is enough if the other details can be provided on request within three working days. The originator is told appropriately that its details are passed on, and the beneficiary's financial intermediary sets on a risk basis how it handles orders with incomplete details.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set criteria for higher-risk business relationships and identify and mark those relationships
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV-FINMA (SR 955.033.0), Art. 13 Abs. 1, 2bis, 3 und 6, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Set criteria for higher-risk business relationships and identify and mark those relationships

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must develop criteria that point to business relationships with higher risks, record on the basis of its risk analysis which of the criteria the ordinance lists are relevant to its business, give them concrete form in internal directives and use them to identify higher-risk relationships. Relationships with foreign politically exposed persons and those close to them, with foreign banks for which it carries out correspondent banking, and with persons resident in a country for which the FATF calls for enhanced due diligence are always higher-risk. It identifies and marks its higher-risk relationships internally.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Have senior management decide on taking up higher-risk relationships and every year on continuing those with politically exposed persons
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV-FINMA (SR 955.033.0), Art. 19 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Have senior management decide on taking up higher-risk relationships and every year on continuing those with politically exposed persons

summaries.en: The most senior management body, or at least one of its members, must decide on taking up the higher-risk business relationships the ordinance names, and every year on continuing relationships with foreign politically exposed persons, domestic and international-organisation politically exposed persons and persons close to them. It also orders regular checks of all higher-risk relationships and their monitoring and evaluation.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Monitor relationships and transactions effectively, at a bank with an IT-based transaction monitoring system
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV-FINMA (SR 955.033.0), Art. 20 Abs. 1 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Monitor relationships and transactions effectively, at a bank with an IT-based transaction monitoring system

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must monitor its business relationships and transactions effectively so that higher risks are identified. Banks and securities firms run an IT-based system that helps identify higher-risk transactions, and evaluate the transactions it flags within a reasonable time with further clarifications where needed; a bank or securities firm with few clients, beneficial owners or transactions may do without the system.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Appoint an anti-money laundering unit and adopt board-approved internal anti-money laundering directives
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV-FINMA (SR 955.033.0), Art. 24 und Art. 26 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Appoint an anti-money laundering unit and adopt board-approved internal anti-money laundering directives

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must appoint one or more qualified persons as its anti-money laundering unit, which supports and advises line managers and executive management, prepares the internal directives and plans and supervises internal training. It issues internal directives on combating money laundering and terrorist financing, adopted by the board of directors or the most senior management body and made known to the persons concerned, which settle in particular the criteria for higher-risk relationships and transactions, transaction monitoring, when the unit and senior management are involved, training, the policy on politically exposed persons, who reports to the reporting office, amount thresholds, the use of third parties and the updating of client documents.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Check that foreign correspondent banks do no business with shell banks, review their controls and pass on complete payment details
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwV-FINMA (SR 955.033.0), Art. 37 Abs. 2 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Check that foreign correspondent banks do no business with shell banks, review their controls and pass on complete payment details

summaries.en: A financial intermediary that carries out correspondent banking for a foreign bank must make sure in a suitable way that the foreign bank may not do business with shell banks and, depending on the circumstances, clarify which anti-money laundering controls the foreign bank applies, taking into account whether it is under adequate supervision. It ensures that the details received for payment orders are complete and passed on, and sets on a risk basis how it proceeds when it repeatedly receives orders with obviously incomplete details.
